topics.name: Human and Machine Contract Dual Representation
topics.purpose: Define the requirement that canonical semantics remain machine-readable while a human-readable representation/prose projection is preserved alongside them.

semantics.machine_rule: Machine-significant semantics are represented structurally in canonical Contract Format fields.
semantics.equivalence_rule: Human projection must not contradict machine-readable semantics.
semantics.authority_rule: Human prose does not override conflicting machine-readable canonical structure unless an explicit change is accepted into the contract.
semantics.generation_rule: Human views may be generated from canonical structure where deterministic.
semantics.roundtrip_rule: Editing human representation requires explicit mapping back to canonical semantics before acceptance.

invariants.rule: Composition never silently transfers semantic ownership: universal modules own their primitives, domains own their composition semantics, and composed members retain their own identities and contracts.

Containment, relation, dependency, composition and projection edges exist only through explicit typed references; naming, file hierarchy, UI adjacency or shared values never create semantic structure.
